name: 13f-scraper
what_it_holds: Scrapes/parses/normalizes SEC 13F filings via CLI and Python API; lookup by fund name, CIK, or CSV upload; outputs CSV (fund name, CIK, filing period, first-time-filer flag, holdings count) and detailed holdings CSV/JSONL. First-time-filer detection, holdings-count filtering, REST API, rate-limited SEC compliance, response caching. MIT license.
why_useful: More feature-complete 13F puller than most (first-time-filer detection is useful for spotting new institutional entrants into ABNB); addresses gap #15.
themes: 13F holdings parsers and institutional-ownership history, short-interest datasets, insider-transaction parsers (Form 4), ETF holdings trackers
why_all: More feature-complete 13F puller than most (first-time-filer detection is useful for spotting new institutional entrants into ABNB); addresses gap #15.

name: pit-fundamentals
what_it_holds: data/pit_fundamentals_history.csv (6,969 rows), plus query_asof.py (point-in-time query tool) and check_your_data.py (lookahead-bias checker). Covers 40 large-cap US companies, 16 financial concepts, each row stamped with period_end, first_filed (public-disclosure date), lag_days, original_value, latest_value, restated flag. ~12 years of revenue history per company. Source: SEC EDGAR (public domain), CC0-licensed. Rebuilt 7 Sep 2026, 36 commits.
why_useful: Directly implements gap #4's method (point-in-time fundamentals with no lookahead bias) as a reusable, license-clean pattern; even if ABNB/OTAs are not among the 40 tickers (unconfirmed), the query_asof.py + methodology is a ready-made PIT harness we could apply to ABNB's own EDGAR filings, which is exactly the discipline our CLAUDE.md rule #2 already requires.
themes: Company KPI and alt-data backtest repos for ABNB or OTAs: anyone who already assembled Airbnb quarterly KPI datasets, consensus, or alt-data panels

name: post-no-preference/earnings (DoltHub)
what_it_holds: A Dolt (git-for-data) database on DoltHub described as holding "historical revenue and EPS estimates... data goes back to 2018 and is recorded weekly" — i.e. weekly-vintage analyst consensus snapshots, versioned like git commits so any past vintage is queryable/diffable. Not on GitHub itself but Dolt repos are git-clonable and DoltHub is a public, free host.
why_useful: If it covers ABNB/BKNG/EXPE, this is close to a direct hit on gap #4 (historical analyst-consensus snapshots with true point-in-time versioning via Dolt's commit history) — worth a follow-up check of ticker coverage since ABNB has only traded since Dec 2020.
